first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent this with 'Mum, look at the champagne one!' so I sat down with the iPad. The opening is plain English, no silly slang, and it says it works for 40 guests as well as 200, which is about where we are. The key points mention weather and power at an overseas venue, so it's not just pretty pictures. I read on.

journey.quote: Treat the display as a sign before it is decor, with clear names, a sensible height and a clear path in front.
journey.reaction: Thank goodness. Someone who understands that half our guests are over seventy and need to actually read the thing.

journey.quote: This one needs staff to pour in time and keep the tray topped up, so arrange it with the venue's bar team. Have a few glasses of something without alcohol ready too.
journey.reaction: This is the one my daughter loves, and I'm glad it says plainly that it needs staff. That's a cost question I'll raise with her. And yes, my mother won't touch champagne.

journey.section: A Screen or QR Lookup on Arrival
journey.quote: Never rely on a phone alone. Some guests will not have one to hand, some will have a flat battery, and signal at a remote venue can be patchy.
journey.reaction: Exactly what I would have said, and I didn't have to be the old-fashioned one who said it. My sister won't be scanning any codes.
I had no idea what this heading meant until I read the paragraph. It's about a photo spot, so why not just say so?

journey.quote: Queensland guidance for events is a sound reference here.
journey.reaction: Fine, it's a government source, which I trust more than a blog. A little odd that it's Queensland when we're in Melbourne and marrying overseas, but the advice is sensible.

journey.quote: Signs should sit apart from other visual clutter and stand out from their surroundings. Displays should be viewable at every height, including by people using wheelchairs, children and taller guests, and tested with a crowd in front before the event.
journey.reaction: Good content, but this paragraph is a long block on the iPad. I had to read it twice. Break it up, please.

journey.quote: Guests with additional needs can be seated early, with staff walking them to their places.
journey.reaction: This is the line I'll forward to my husband. My mother uses a walking frame, and the thought of her shuffling through a crowd at the entrance worries me. Seating her early is the answer.

journey.quote: In practice, that means an interactive display should never be the only way to find a seat. Keep a printed list at a seated reading height, and ask a host or a member of the bridal party to stand nearby for the first half hour.
journey.reaction: Practical and kind. A real person standing there is what makes me relax.

journey.quote: give one person the master list on the day so every change goes through them.
journey.reaction: One person responsible. That's how I'd run it too.

journey.section: Interactive Seating Charts at a Destination Wedding
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, so these answers are settled before the design is.
journey.reaction: In writing, before we commit. That's the sentence I was looking for. It still doesn't tell me about deposits or what happens if the venue's people don't turn up, but it's a start.

journey.section: Plan It with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Advisor works in your time zone and plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world.
journey.reaction: Works in our time zone answers half my 2am question. 'Payments' makes me want to know more: are deposits protected, and is it all quoted in Australian dollars?

unanswered_questions: Can I speak to the Wedded Advisor on the phone before anything is booked?
If the Advisor handles payments, are deposits paid to overseas venues and suppliers protected, and who is responsible if a supplier lets us down?
Will quotes be in Australian dollars, and will venue contracts be in English?
Who do we ring on the wedding day itself, at the venue, if the setup goes wrong?
Is the Wedded Concierge service charged separately, and is that fee agreed in writing?
Does the Advisor check the venue's access for older guests (steps, terraces, path to the reception) or is that left to us?

turn_offs_found.quote: Signs should sit apart from other visual clutter and stand out from their surroundings. Displays should be viewable at every height, including by people using wheelchairs, children and taller guests, and tested with a crowd in front before the event.
turn_offs_found.why: Part of a long, unbroken paragraph that is hard going on an iPad. The content is good, the layout isn't.
Vague, slightly trendy heading that doesn't say what the section is about.

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Advisor works in your time zone and plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world.
turn_offs_found.why: Mentions payments but nothing on deposits or accountability for overseas suppliers, my biggest fear. (Deferred business detail, not a blocker.)

would_share_with: My husband (the accessibility section and the line about the Advisor confirming inclusions in writing)
My sister, who is helping with the table plan (the alphabetical or by table section)

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready to talk it through, start a conversation with [Wedded Concierge]
cta_reaction.why: 'Talk it through' sounds like a phone call, which is what I want, and the written inclusions line helps. But this is a seating chart article, so I'd leave the first enquiry to my daughter and ask to be on the call. I'd want deposits and AUD quotes covered then.

top_3_changes: Rename the vague heading. Old: "### The Art of Technology" New: "### A Seating Display That Doubles as a Photo Spot"

Split the long accessibility paragraph for easier reading on a tablet. Old: "<!-- fact_05 --> Displays should be viewable at every height" New: "<!-- fact_05 -->\n\nDisplays should be viewable at every height"

Name older guests in the practical summary so the paying parent feels seen, without new facts. Old: "Keep a printed list at a seated reading height, and ask a host or a member of the bridal party to stand nearby for the first half hour." New: "Keep a printed list at a seated reading height for older guests and anyone using a wheelchair, and ask a host or a member of the bridal party to stand nearby for the first half hour."
